1) If they ignore your email  
- Give them a specific window in the first email (e.g., “within 5 business days”).

Subject: Second Request – Refund for Dec 1 Plumbing Service

I’m following up on my message sent on [date] regarding the Dec 1 plumbing service at my home in Houston (toilet still leaking, mess left behind, nearly 2-hour late arrival without proper notice).

I haven’t received a response yet. Please confirm within 3 business days whether you will:
- Issue a full refund to my original payment method, or
- Provide a no-cost re-do with a different technician by [reasonable date].

If I don’t hear back, I’ll have to escalate this through my credit card company and, if needed, other consumer channels.

Thank you,  
Danielle Kim

If they still ignore you after that, move to your credit card company (see step 3).

2) If they respond but say “no refund”  
Ask for their position in writing and keep it. Then reply briefly, focusing on facts:

- The leak is still present (service not completed as promised).  
- They left your bathroom in worse condition (mess/cleanup).  
- They were ~2 hours late without proper notice, which affects “professional service” standards.

You can respond with something like:

Hi [Name],

I appreciate the response, but I don’t agree with your decision.

The original problem (toilet leak) remains, meaning the service was not successfully completed. In addition, the technician left dirty water and trash behind, and arrived almost 2 hours late without proper notice.

Given those issues, I still believe a full refund is appropriate. If we can’t resolve this directly, I’ll have to dispute the charge with my credit card company and share our correspondence and documentation with them.

Danielle Kim

After this, you’re in a good position to escalate.

3) Disputing the charge with your credit card  
Call the number on the back of your card or log in online and look for “Dispute a charge” or “Billing dispute.”

When you file the dispute, be ready with:
- Date of service: Dec 1, 2025  
- Amount charged and merchant name  
- Description: “Service not as described / defective service” (toilet still leaks, mess, lateness)  
- Evidence:
  - Photos or video of the ongoing leak  
  - Any photos or description of the mess (and notes on what you had to clean)  
  - Your original appointment time vs. actual arrival time (texts/emails if any)  
  - Copy of your first and follow-up emails to the company  
  - Any response from the company refusing a refund

When talking to the credit card company, you can say something like:

“I’d like to dispute a charge for a plumbing service on Dec 1, 2025. The main problem was not fixed (toilet is still leaking), the technician left the bathroom dirty, and they arrived nearly 2 hours late with poor communication. I tried to resolve this directly with the company on my own and requested a refund on [dates], but they [did not respond / refused]. I have emails, photos, and documentation I can provide.”

They’ll tell you how to upload or send your documentation. Make sure you:
- Respond promptly to any requests they make.  
- Keep all your notes and emails together in a single folder (digital or printed).

4) Optional: local escalation if needed  
If the chargeback doesn’t work or you want more leverage:
- You can file a complaint with your city or state consumer protection agency or Better Business Bureau (BBB), especially if they’re clearly refusing to address unfinished work.  
- Leave a factual review describing what happened (after you’ve finished disputes; keep it calm and specific).

If you want, tell me:
- Roughly how much the job cost, and  
- Whether you already have photos/video of the leak,

and I can tailor a very short, point-by-point “case summary” you can reuse for the credit card dispute form or any complaints you file.</action>
